lessons.title: Bonjour l'art!
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize art exists everywhere around them

opening.activity: Circle time greeting with art objects. Show 3-4 familiar items (crayon, picture book, decorated pencil case). Point and say 'Voici l'art!' Use big gestures and excited voice. Students repeat with actions.

closing.activity: Art Gallery Share. Students place their chosen art object on desk. Walk around like in an art gallery, whispering 'Je vois...' and naming colors they see. End with group cheer: 'L'art est partout!' (Art is everywhere!)

troubleshooting.then: Picture book art hunt: Use any picture book, point to illustrations saying 'Voici l'art!' Students find colors and repeat vocabulary. Works with any adult, no French required.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Looking for art in their bedroom, kitchen, playground - send home simple visual checklist with pictures

lessons.title: Mes yeux découvrent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will use their eyes to observe details in their environment

opening.activity: Review game with Lesson 1 vocabulary using actions. Then introduce 'regarder' with exaggerated looking gesture (hand above eyes like binoculars). Practice looking at ceiling, floor, each other with 'Je regarde...'

closing.activity: Detail Gallery Walk. Post drawings on board. Students walk by and point to details they can identify, saying 'Je vois un détail!' or 'Une forme!' End with group celebration of their detective eyes.

troubleshooting.then: Shape puppet show: Use any geometric shapes (blocks, cut paper). Make shapes 'talk' to each other in simple French. Students identify and respond to shapes. No art background needed.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Noticing shapes in clouds, patterns on clothing, textures on playground - encourage 'detective eyes' at home and recess

lessons.title: J'aime, j'aime pas
lessons.oneGoal: Students will express simple preferences about visual things they see

opening.activity: Show two contrasting art pieces (bright vs dark, busy vs simple). Model preferences with clear gestures: 'J'aime!' (thumbs up, smile) and 'J'aime pas!' (gentle shake of head). Students practice with hand gestures for each phrase.

materials: Two easels or wall spaces for voting activity

closing.activity: Preference Circle. Students sit with their 'beau' object from hunt. Each shares: 'J'aime...' and points to their object. Others respond with 'C'est beau!' End with 'Nos goûts sont différents!' (Our tastes are different!)

troubleshooting.then: Picture book preferences: Use any picture book with varied illustrations. Point to different pages asking 'J'aime ou j'aime pas?' Students show thumbs up/down. Celebrate all answers as valid opinions.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Choosing favorite toys, clothes, or foods based on how they look - encourage family conversations about preferences

lessons.title: Mes mains créent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore basic art materials safely and confidently

opening.activity: Hand warm-up with finger wiggles and 'magic hands' gestures. Introduce vocabulary with TPR: hold up 'crayon' and pretend to draw, wave 'papier' like a flag, use both hands in creating motion for 'créer'. Students mirror all actions.

materials: Simple smocks or paper towels for cleanup

closing.activity: Creator Circle. Students hold their creation and share: 'J'ai créé avec...' (holding up their crayon type). Others celebrate: 'Bravo! Tu crées!' Practice putting materials away properly saying 'Merci, crayon!' to each tool.

troubleshooting.then: Paper sculpture: Use any paper available. Show simple folding, rolling, tearing techniques. Students experiment saying 'Je crée' with each action. No drawing skills needed, focus on manipulation.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Drawing pictures for family, decorating their room, making cards - encourage trying different papers and crayons at home

lessons.title: Lignes partout!
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create different types of lines with purpose

opening.activity: Body lines: Students make straight lines with arms ('droite' - arms out straight), curved lines with bodies ('courbe' - bend and sway). Draw lines in air following teacher. Use whole body to understand 'ligne' concept with movement.

closing.activity: Line Gallery. Post artwork at student eye level. Walk gallery style, students point to different line types they see: 'Je vois une ligne droite!' Celebrate variety and effort with specific praise about line choices.

troubleshooting.then: Finger line tracing: Use any textbook or worksheet with printed lines (letters, borders, pictures). Students trace over lines with fingers, identifying 'droite' or 'courbe'. Requires no art supplies.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Lines in sidewalk cracks, tree branches, their own hair - notice and name line types during outdoor play and daily routines

lessons.title: Formes magiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize and create basic shapes in art

opening.activity: Shape actions: Draw shapes in air while saying names. 'Cercle' - arms make big circle, 'carré' - four-cornered gesture with index fingers, 'triangle' - three-pointed shape with arms above head. Students mirror and chant shape names.

materials: Chart paper and markers for tally
Crayons and paper for individual work

closing.activity: Shape Gallery Share. Students display their magic shape art and identify what shapes they used: 'J'ai utilisé des cercles!' (I used circles!) Others guess what they see in the shape art: 'Je vois un soleil!' (I see a sun!)

troubleshooting.then: Shape sorting: Use any classroom manipulatives (blocks, books, supplies). Sort into shape categories while practicing French names. Students take turns being 'shape caller' - no drawing required.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Shapes in their house windows, food, toys, and books - family shape hunting game at home with simple checklist

lessons.title: Couleurs vivantes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will use color intentionally to express ideas

opening.activity: Color energy movement: 'Rouge' - stomp like fire, 'bleu' - flow like water, 'jaune' - bounce like sunshine. Students mirror movements while chanting color names. Show how colors can have personalities and feelings.

closing.activity: Color Intention Share. Students explain their color choices: 'J'ai choisi le rouge pour...' (I chose red for...). Others listen and respond with color connections: 'Le rouge me fait penser à...' (Red makes me think of...)

troubleshooting.then: Color story: Tell simple story using only color words and gestures. Students act out different colors as characters. 'Rouge was angry, Bleu was sad, Jaune came to make everyone happy!' No art supplies needed.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Colors in nature, their favorite foods, seasonal changes - discuss how colors make them feel in different situations at home

lessons.title: Textures à toucher
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore how texture can be shown in art

opening.activity: Texture box mystery: Without looking, students feel objects of different textures. Describe with actions: 'doux' - gentle pet motion, 'rugueux' - scratchy clawing motion, 'toucher' - reaching out with fingertips. Guess and reveal objects.

materials: Texture sample collection (sandpaper, cotton, fabric, bubble wrap)

closing.activity: Texture Gallery Walk. Students touch each other's texture artwork (gently!) and identify what they feel: 'Je touche... c'est doux!' Partner discussions about texture choices and techniques used.

troubleshooting.then: Classroom texture hunt: Find smooth and rough surfaces around room (desk tops, carpet, walls). Students touch and categorize using French texture words. No art supplies needed, just exploration.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Feeling bark on trees, smooth stones, fuzzy sweaters - encourage texture awareness during outdoor play and daily activities

lessons.title: Mes sentiments en art
lessons.oneGoal: Students will connect their emotions to their artistic choices

opening.activity: Emotion mirror: Teacher shows emotion faces and students mirror while saying French words. 'Content' - big smile and relaxed shoulders, 'triste' - sad face and drooping posture, 'excité' - bouncy energy and wide eyes. Practice transitioning between emotions.

closing.activity: Emotion Art Share. Students hold artwork and share their emotion choice: 'Mon art montre que je suis content!' Others respond supportively: 'Je comprends ton sentiment!' (I understand your feeling!)

troubleshooting.then: Emotion charades: Students act out emotions while others guess in French. Then discuss what colors or lines might show those emotions. No art supplies needed, focus on expression and vocabulary.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Happy birthday drawings, comfort objects, celebrating achievements - encourage expressing feelings through art at home during different moods

lessons.title: Outils d'artiste
lessons.oneGoal: Students will select appropriate tools for their artistic intentions

opening.activity: Tool parade: Hold up each tool type with exaggerated demonstration. 'Pinceau' - painting gestures in air, 'colle' - sticky finger motions, 'ciseaux' - cutting actions (safety emphasis). Students practice motions while chanting tool names.

closing.activity: Artist Tool Talk. Students show their multi-tool artwork and explain which tools they used: 'J'ai utilisé les ciseaux pour...' Others ask questions: 'Pourquoi le pinceau?' Tool cleanup becomes vocabulary practice.

troubleshooting.then: Tool pantomime: Students act out using different art tools while others guess in French. Discuss what each tool does best. No actual tools needed, focus on understanding tool purposes.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Choosing right tools for jobs at home, helping with crafts - encourage noticing when family members select specific tools for different tasks

lessons.title: Techniques nouvelles
lessons.oneGoal: Students will try new art techniques to achieve different effects

opening.activity: Technique demonstrations: Show each new technique with exaggerated actions. 'Mélanger' - stirring/mixing motions, 'tamponner' - dabbing/stamping actions, 'gratter' - gentle scratching movements. Students practice motions in air while learning pronunciation.

closing.activity: Technique Gallery. Students explain which technique they chose and why: 'J'ai préféré mélanger parce que...' Others observe technique effects in different artworks. Celebrate variety of choices and discoveries made.

troubleshooting.then: Technique storytelling: Tell story of three artist friends who each had special technique. Students act out techniques while story progresses. No art supplies needed, focus on understanding and movement.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Different ways to spread jam, clean windows, or play in sand - connect art techniques to daily activities that use similar motions

lessons.title: Mon style unique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize their own artistic preferences and style

opening.activity: Style celebration: Look at student artwork from previous lessons. Point out different approaches: 'Voici le style de...' Emphasize that different is wonderful. Students practice saying 'Mon style est unique!' with proud gestures.

closing.activity: Style Celebration Circle. Students share one thing that makes their style special: 'Mon style est spécial parce que...' Others respond with appreciation: 'Ton style est unique!' End with group cheer about everyone being special artists.

troubleshooting.then: Style dress-up: Students describe their clothing style choices using French vocabulary. Connect to artistic style: 'My clothes are bright like my art!' No art supplies needed, personal connection.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Their unique way of decorating, dressing, or arranging their space - encourage family conversations about what makes each person special

lessons.title: Partager mes idées
lessons.oneGoal: Students will communicate about their art using French vocabulary learned

opening.activity: Communication practice: Teacher models different ways to share art. 'Expliquer' - pointing and describing, 'montrer' - displaying and indicating features, 'raconter' - telling story about the art. Students practice each gesture style.

closing.activity: Communication Celebration. Students vote for different communication awards: 'Meilleure explication' (best explanation), 'Meilleure histoire' (best story), 'Meilleure présentation' (best presentation). Everyone gets recognized for something special.

troubleshooting.then: Show and tell circle: Students simply show artwork and say one French word about it. Others repeat the word and clap. Focus on vocabulary reinforcement over complex communication.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Showing family their creations, explaining their room decorations - encourage practicing French art words when sharing at home

lessons.title: Art dans ma vie
lessons.oneGoal: Students will demonstrate understanding of how art connects to their daily experience

opening.activity: Daily art hunt: Students think about their morning routine and identify art they saw/used: clothing patterns, cereal box designs, toothbrush colors. Practice vocabulary: 'L'art est important dans ma vie quotidienne!' (Art is important in my daily life!)

closing.activity: Art Life Commitment. Students share one way they will use art in their daily life: 'L'art va être important dans ma vie parce que...' Create class commitment to noticing and creating art every day.

troubleshooting.then: Art gratitude circle: Students say 'Merci' to different art elements in the classroom, explaining why: 'Merci, couleurs, parce que vous me rendez heureux!' Focus on appreciation and vocabulary.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Making art part of their daily routine, noticing design everywhere - encourage family discussions about art in their home and community

lessons.title: Atelier libre
lessons.oneGoal: Students will practice all learned techniques in self-directed creation

opening.activity: Art vocabulary review game: Students take turns acting out vocabulary words from lessons 1-14 while others guess in French. Quick energy builder that reinforces all learned terms before independent work time.

materials: All art materials from previous lessons available

closing.activity: Artist Reflection. Students complete sentence starters: 'Aujourd'hui j'ai utilisé...' (Today I used...) 'Ma technique préférée était...' (My favorite technique was...) 'Je suis fier de...' (I'm proud of...)

troubleshooting.then: Free choice art using only available classroom supplies (pencils, paper, classroom decorations for inspiration). Focus on creativity and vocabulary use rather than specific materials.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Having art time at home, making gifts, decorating personal spaces - encourage establishing regular creative time in daily routine

lessons.title: Collaboration artistique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will work together on artistic projects using learned vocabulary

opening.activity: Collaboration warm-up: Partner mirror drawing - one student draws while partner mirrors movements in air. Practice sharing materials and space. Introduce collaboration phrases: 'On peut partager?' (Can we share?) 'Bonne idée!' (Good idea!)

closing.activity: Collaboration Celebration. Groups present their collaborative work, explaining how they worked together: 'Nous avons collaboré en...' (We collaborated by...) Others appreciate: 'Votre collaboration est belle!' (Your collaboration is beautiful!)

troubleshooting.then: Collaborative storytelling: Students take turns adding to visual story on board using simple drawings while practicing French vocabulary. No individual supplies needed.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Making art with siblings, friends, or family members - encourage collaborative creative projects at home

lessons.title: Art en grand
lessons.oneGoal: Students will apply their skills to larger-scale creative projects

opening.activity: Scale exploration: Compare small and large versions of same artwork. Discuss challenges and opportunities of working big: 'En grand, je peux...' (When working big, I can...) Practice big gestures and movements for large-scale art.

materials: Large format paper (poster size or larger)
Floor space or large table areas

closing.activity: Scale Reflection. Students compare their large-scale work experience with smaller projects: 'Travailler en grand était...' (Working big was...) 'J'ai appris que...' (I learned that...) Discuss challenges and successes.

troubleshooting.then: Floor art: Use chalk or washable markers on floor tiles (if available) to create large-scale temporary art. Focus on big movements and scale adaptation.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Decorating their bedroom, making posters, creating gifts for family - encourage thinking about scale in home projects

lessons.title: Galerie de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will curate and present their artwork in a gallery setting

opening.activity: Gallery visit preparation: Discuss how art galleries work. Practice gallery behavior: quiet voices, careful looking, respectful comments. Introduce curatorial vocabulary: 'Je choisis cette œuvre parce que...' (I choose this work because...)

materials: All student artwork from previous lessons

closing.activity: Gallery Reflection. Students complete gallery visitor forms: 'Mon œuvre préférée était...' (My favorite work was...) 'J'ai appris...' (I learned...) 'La galerie m'a fait sentir...' (The gallery made me feel...)

troubleshooting.then: Desk gallery: Each student creates mini gallery on their desk with 2-3 small artworks. Others visit desk galleries in small groups, practicing vocabulary and respectful viewing.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Displaying their art at home, choosing what to show to visitors - encourage creating personal art displays in their rooms

lessons.title: Art et nature
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create art inspired by natural elements and materials

opening.activity: Nature art exploration: Show examples of natural materials used in art (leaf printing, stone painting, twig sculptures). Discuss respectful collection: 'Nous prenons seulement ce que nous avons besoin' (We take only what we need). Practice nature vocabulary review.

closing.activity: Nature Art Share. Students present their nature art explaining their inspiration: 'La nature m'inspire parce que...' (Nature inspires me because...) 'J'ai utilisé...' (I used...) Connect to environmental appreciation.

troubleshooting.then: Nature drawing from observation: Use any plants visible from classroom windows or indoor plants. Students practice observational drawing while using descriptive vocabulary.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Collecting leaves and flowers, rock painting, nature photography - encourage respectful nature appreciation and creation at home

lessons.title: Célébration artistique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will celebrate their artistic growth and share with families

opening.activity: Growth reflection: Students look through portfolio of work from all lessons. Identify improvements and new skills: 'Au début, je...' (At the beginning, I...) 'Maintenant, je peux...' (Now I can...) Celebrate progress with encouraging gestures.

closing.activity: Artist Commitment Circle. Students share one artistic goal for the future: 'Je veux continuer à...' (I want to continue to...) 'L'art va toujours être important parce que...' (Art will always be important because...) Group celebration of artistic growth.

troubleshooting.then: Art appreciation circle: Students take turns appreciating something special about each classmate's artistic development using French vocabulary. Focus on community celebration and individual recognition.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Continuing to make art at home, noticing art everywhere, sharing creativity - encourage lifelong artistic engagement and French vocabulary use
